---
title: "Reproduce"
---

This chapter walks through reproducing every flavor of run the harness
supports: a single prompt, a convergence study, a full sweep, and
inspecting the results. All commands assume you have already followed
[Setup](setup.qmd).

## End-to-end reproduction

The shortest path from clone to rendered plots:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HrudithL/gt-skill && cd gt-skill
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install claude-agent-sdk great_tables pandas python-dotenv anyio pillow anthropic plotnine
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
echo 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...' > .env

python scripts/fetch_data.py               # provision data/*.csv
python run.py --skill scripts --difficulty easy --repeat 3
```

That last command triggers a full easy-difficulty sweep under the
scripted skill, with three with-skill samples per prompt plus a
baseline. It produces one run tree that has everything downstream
tools need to render the [comparator plots](methodology.qmd#the-comparator).

## A single prompt

Fastest thing you can do to verify the install works and to eyeball
what one output looks like.

```bash
python run.py --skill prose --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
```

Output:

```
runs/single/<ts>_prose_sp500_monthly_performance/
  run.json
  summary.json
  prompts/
    sp500_monthly_performance/
      repeat_1/
        table.py
        table.png
        transcript.json
        data/sp500.csv -> ../../../../data/sp500.csv
        .claude/skills/great-tables/
```

Open `table.png` — that's the table the skill produced. Read
`transcript.json` to see what the agent did to get there.

## A convergence run

Convergence tells you how consistent the skill is across samples on
the *same* prompt. Any variant supports it; just add `--repeat N`.

```bash
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt sp500_monthly_performance --repeat 3
```

Output adds `convergence.json` + `contact_sheet.png` at the prompt
level, plus one `baseline/` directory (baseline is auto-enabled when
`--repeat > 1`):

```
runs/convergence/<ts>_scripts_sp500_monthly_performance/
  prompts/sp500_monthly_performance/
    baseline/
    repeat_1/  repeat_2/  repeat_3/
    convergence.json
    contact_sheet.png
```

`convergence.json` is the machine-readable report; `contact_sheet.png`
composites the three rendered tables side by side so you can eyeball
whether the parser's agreement fraction actually corresponds to visual
similarity.

## A full sweep

The sweep is the workhorse for measuring a skill against the corpus.

```bash
python run.py --skill scripts --difficulty easy --repeat 3
```

Output tree:

```
runs/sweep/<ts>_scripts_multi/
  run.json                                   # RunSpec + resolved config
  summary.json                               # aggregate pass/fail + tokens/cost
  prompts/
    <prompt-1>/  <prompt-2>/  <prompt-3>/... # one dir per easy corpus prompt
      baseline/  repeat_1/  repeat_2/  repeat_3/
      convergence.json
      contact_sheet.png
```

Swap `--difficulty easy` for `--difficulty all` to sweep every corpus
prompt. Swap `--model haiku` for `sonnet` or `opus` (or any raw
`claude-*` id) to trade cost for quality.

Per-invocation cost estimate: `--repeat 3` + auto-baseline = 4 agent
invocations per prompt + up to 4 judge calls per prompt. Multiply by
the number of prompts in the difficulty bucket, then by your model's
per-invocation cost. `run.py` prints the total invocation count up
front (`invocations: 24`) so you can spot-check before running.

## Inspecting results

Every run leaves everything on disk. Key files:

- **`run.json`** — the `RunSpec`, the resolved config, per-step
  timings, and the run status. Machine-readable.
- **`summary.json`** — aggregate pass/fail, total tokens, total cost.
  Machine-readable.
- **`prompts/<name>/{baseline,repeat_N}/table.png`** — the rendered
  tables. Look at these.
- **`prompts/<name>/{baseline,repeat_N}/transcript.json`** — the SDK
  conversation. Useful for understanding *why* the model made a
  choice.
- **`prompts/<name>/{baseline,repeat_N}/report.txt`** — the
  comparator score, if the prompt has a ground truth. See
  [Methodology / The comparator](methodology.qmd#the-comparator).
- **`prompts/<name>/contact_sheet.png`** — for convergence runs, all
  N samples side by side.

To render the per-skill plots (`comparator_score.png`, `usage.png`)
from a completed sweep, use `eval-results/_plots.py` — it consumes a
sweep's `runs/sweep/<...>` and writes plots into `eval-results-demo/`.
That script is tracked; the surrounding `eval-results/` and
`eval-results-demo/` directories are gitignored per the [production
polish plan](https://github.com/HrudithL/gt-skill/pull/122) so raw
artifacts stay local to your machine.

## Cost sanity checks

The runner will not silently spend money. Two guardrails:

1. `RunSpec.invocation_count()` is printed at the top of every run,
   before any Chrome launch or API call, so a mistyped
   `--repeat 30` fails obvious.
2. Bad data paths / missing API keys / empty prompt selections fail
   with exit code `2` **before** the sidecar starts. You cannot get
   billed for a run that was never going to complete.

If a run does start and needs to be killed, `Ctrl-C` is safe — the
sidecar teardown removes the profile directory, and every completed
invocation's transcript is already flushed to disk.
